new_packages.justification: This Torah contains explicit bechina language connecting 3+ concepts in an independent domain not found in the dataset. The language 'יֵשׁ אֵצֶל הַצַּדִּיק בְּחִינַת עָלִין וַעֲנָפִים' is paradigmatic bechina syntax. The tree-organism metaphor for the tzaddik is a coherent, self-contained thematic domain. The cross-reference to Torah 66 confirms this is an established structural metaphor in the corpus. The package is entirely absent from torahData.js and must be created from scratch.

observations:
Torah 224 is a short, focused teaching (2 sentences) that is entirely unprocessed in the dataset — it has zero edges in torahData.js. The teaching consists of a single sustained bechina: the tzaddik is like a tree (הַצַּדִּיק כְּבְחִינַת אִילָן). The tree's structural components (branches, bark, leaves) are each declared a bechina of aspects of the tzaddik. The distant grasses are declared the bechina of the distant human souls. This is unmistakably a package-generating Torah with one clear package: צַּדִּיק וְאִילָן.

Why NEW_PACKAGES_PROPOSED and not NO_NEW_PACKAGES:
1. The source text has explicit bechina language ('יֵשׁ אֵצֶל הַצַּדִּיק בְּחִינַת עָלִין וַעֲנָפִים') connecting multiple nodes.
2. The tzaddik-as-tree domain is a coherent, independent thematic cluster not covered by any existing Torah 224 packages (there are none).
3. There are at minimum 4 bechina pairs identifiable directly from the text: (a) tzaddik ~ tree, (b) tzaddik ~ branches/leaves, (c) distant grasses ~ distant people, (d) covering/protecting ~ mode of vitality-transmission.
4. The cross-reference to Torah 66 (where the branches/leaves metaphor is developed more fully) confirms this is a recognized structural bechina in the corpus.

Note on good/evil mirror: This Torah has no developed evil counterpart. The sun (שמש) is mentioned as the threat from which the tree protects the distant grasses, but it is not developed into a full evil package. The teaching is entirely positive: it reassures that even the spiritually distant receive the tzaddik's vitality through his covering/sheltering activity.
